l1: What Windows version and build is the affected client running? Verify with: Get-ComputerInfo | Select WindowsProductName, WindowsVersion, OsHardwareAbstractionLayer

What IP address is the client currently showing — APIPA (169.254.x.x), an IP from the wrong scope, or no IP at all? Check with: Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where IPAddress -notlike '127.*' | Select InterfaceAlias,IPAddress,PrefixOrigin
Is the DHCP Client service (Dhcp) running on the affected machine? Verify with: Get-Service Dhcp | Select Name,Status,StartType,DependentServices
Is this a wired Ethernet connection, Wi-Fi connection, or a virtual NIC (Hyper-V/VMware)? Identify with: Get-NetAdapter | Where Status -eq 'Up' | Select Name,InterfaceDescription,MediaType,Virtual

Is the issue intermittent (e.g., fails after wake from sleep) or persistent (never receives an IP)? For intermittent issues, check: Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-Dhcp-Client/Operational -MaxEvents 50 | Where Id -eq 1003
Is the client domain-joined — if so, can it authenticate to the domain when it does receive an IP? Verify with: (Get-WmiObject Win32_ComputerSystem).PartOfDomain and Test-ComputerSecureChannel
Are multiple clients on the same subnet/VLAN affected, or is this one device only? If multiple, investigate DHCP server scope health: Get-DhcpServerv4Scope -ComputerName <DHCP_Server>

Was there a recent change that could explain the problem — NIC driver update, OS upgrade, VLAN reassignment, or Hyper-V VM migration? Check driver: Get-NetAdapter | Select Name,DriverVersion,DriverDate

Does manually assigning a static IP in the same subnet restore full network connectivity — confirming the issue is DHCP-specific? Test with: New-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias '<adapter>' -IPAddress <static_ip> -PrefixLength <mask> -DefaultGateway <gateway>
l2: Does the client have a DHCP reservation configured by MAC address on the DHCP server — is the reservation in the correct scope? Verify with: Get-DhcpServerv4Reservation -ComputerName <DHCP_Server> -ScopeId <scope>
Is the client sending the expected Vendor Class Identifier (Option 60 / VCI) that DHCP policies filter on? Capture with netsh trace and analyze Option 60 in DHCPDISCOVER packets

Is DHCPv6 (IA_NA or IA_PD) being requested alongside DHCPv4 — is the client getting a valid IPv6 address from DHCPv6? Check with: Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv6 | Select InterfaceAlias,IPAddress,PrefixOrigin,SuffixOrigin

Are UDP ports 67 (server-bound) and 68 (client-bound) blocked by Windows Filtering Platform, Windows Firewall, or a network ACL? Verify with: Get-NetFirewallRule | Where {($_.DisplayName -like '*DHCP*') -or ($_.DisplayName -like '*67*') -or ($_.DisplayName -like '*68*')}

For Hyper-V VMs: is the virtual switch type correct (External) — is MAC address spoofing enabled if needed for load balancing or VMs with multiple NICs? Check with: Get-VMSwitch | Select Name,SwitchType,NetAdapterInterfaceDescription and Get-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName <VM> | Select MacAddressSpoofing

Is IPv6 SLAAC autoconfiguring an address that interferes with expected DHCPv6 server-assigned addressing? Verify with: Get-NetIPv6Protocol | Select UseTemporaryAddresses,RandomizeIdentifiers and check Router Advertisement settings

Is there a third-party network management agent or endpoint security product that takes ownership of the NIC and may suppress DHCP requests? Check with: Get-WmiObject Win32_NetworkAdapterConfiguration | Where DHCPEnabled -eq $false and Get-Process | Where Company -match '(Cisco|Palo Alto|Fortinet|Symantec|McAfee)'

For post-sleep/hibernate lease renewal failures: is NIC Wake-on-LAN or power management configured to allow the NIC to remain active through power state transitions? Check with: Get-NetAdapterPowerManagement | Select Name,AllowComputerToTurnOffDevice,WakeOnMagicPacket,WakeOnPattern

l1: Run 'ipconfig /all' — share DHCP Enabled (Yes/No), IP Address, Subnet Mask, Default Gateway, DHCP Server, DNS Servers, Lease Obtained, and Lease Expires fields. For PowerShell equivalent: Get-NetIPConfiguration -Detailed

Run 'ipconfig /release && ipconfig /renew' — share the complete output including any error: 'An error occurred while renewing interface...' PowerShell alternative: Release-lease: Remove-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 -Confirm:$false; Renew: Invoke-Expression 'ipconfig /renew'
Run 'Get-Service Dhcp | Select Name,Status,StartType,DependentServices' — verify service is running and set to Automatic. If stopped, start with: Start-Service Dhcp

Run 'Get-NetIPAddress | Select InterfaceAlias,AddressFamily,IPAddress,PrefixOrigin,SuffixOrigin,AddressState' — check PrefixOrigin should be 'Dhcp' for DHCP-assigned addresses, 'WellKnown' for APIPA (169.254.x.x)
Try a different physical switchport — does the client receive an IP from a different port? This isolates port-specific VLAN or 802.1X authentication issues
Run 'arp -a' — are there duplicate IP-to-MAC mappings indicating an IP address conflict? PowerShell equivalent: Get-NetNeighbor -State Reachable,Stale | Select IPAddress,LinkLayerAddress,State
Restart the network adapter: 'Restart-NetAdapter -Name "<adapter>" -Confirm:$false' — forces NIC reset and fresh DHCP DISCOVER. Identify adapter with: Get-NetAdapter | Where Status -eq 'Up'
l2: Capture DHCP DORA (Discover-Offer-Request-Acknowledge) sequence: 'netsh trace start capture=yes tracefile=C:\dhcp_client_trace.etl' — run 'ipconfig /renew' — 'netsh trace stop' — share ETL for analysis with Message Analyzer or Network Monitor
Run 'Get-NetAdapter | Select Name,Status,MacAddress,LinkSpeed,DriverVersion,DriverDate,InterfaceDescription' — verify driver is current and link speed matches expected (e.g., 1Gbps for gigabit)
Run 'Get-NetAdapterPowerManagement | Select Name,AllowComputerToTurnOffDevice,WakeOnMagicPacket,WakeOnPattern' — power management settings can cause post-sleep DHCP failures
Check Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) for UDP 67/68 blocks: 'netsh wfp show filters | Select-String -Pattern "67|68|dhcp" -Context 2,2' — WFP callouts from security software can block DHCP traffic

On the DHCP server: 'Get-DhcpServerv4Lease -ScopeId <scope> | Where ClientId -eq "<MAC address>"' — confirm whether a lease exists and its state (Active, Expired, Declined). If Windows Server DHCP: Add-DhcpServerInDC to verify authorization

Run 'Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-Dhcp-Client/Operational | Sort TimeCreated -Descending | Select -First 30 | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message' — key events: 1001 (initialized), 1003 (lease obtained), 1006 (lease expired), 1007 (failed to obtain), 1013 (APIPA address assigned)

Run 'Get-NetAdapterBinding -Name "<adapter>" | Select DisplayName,ComponentID,Enabled' — confirm DHCP-relevant bindings (ms_tcpip, ms_tcpip6) are enabled. Re-enable if needed: Enable-NetAdapterBinding -Name '<adapter>' -ComponentID ms_tcpip

For Hyper-V VMs: 'Get-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName <VM> | Select Name,MacAddress,MacAddressSpoofing,Connected,SwitchName,VlanSetting' — verify External switch type and MAC spoofing if using NIC teaming or load balancers

l1: Restart DHCP Client service: 'Restart-Service Dhcp' — verify it restarts successfully with: Get-Service Dhcp | Select Status. Set to Automatic if needed: Set-Service Dhcp -StartupType Automatic

Full release/flush/renew: 'ipconfig /release && ipconfig /flushdns && ipconfig /renew' — PowerShell equivalent: Remove-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 -Confirm:$false; Clear-DnsClientCache; Invoke-Expression 'ipconfig /renew'
Verify the IP Helper address on the router/L3 switch for the client's VLAN points to the correct DHCP server IP. On Cisco: 'show ip helper-address' — on Windows Server RRAS: Get-Service RemoteAccess

Update the NIC driver to the latest version from the hardware OEM — driver bugs can cause DHCP failures. Use Windows Update or OEM website. Verify with: Get-NetAdapter | Select Name,DriverVersion,DriverDate
Check for VLAN mismatch on the switchport — confirm the access VLAN matches the DHCP scope's subnet. On client, verify with: Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name '<adapter>' -RegistryKeyword 'VLANID'

Check for rogue DHCP servers: 'Get-DhcpServerInDC' lists authorized servers in Active Directory. Capture DHCPOFFER responses with Wireshark or Message Analyzer to identify unauthorized servers. Use DHCP Guard in Hyper-V: Set-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName <VM> -RouterGuard On
l2: If DHCP DISCOVER frames are not reaching the server: use pktmon on the client to confirm DISCOVER is being sent — 'pktmon filter add -p 68; pktmon start --capture; ipconfig /renew; pktmon stop'. Analyze with: pktmon format C:\pktmon.etl -o C:\pktmon.txt

If client receives DHCPOFFER but no DHCPREQUEST is sent: check for duplicate IP detection logic in the client — 'Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty | Where DisplayName -like "*ARP*"'. Disable Gratuitous ARP if causing issues: Set-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name '<adapter>' -DisplayName '*Arp*' -DisplayValue 0

For Hyper-V VMs: enable MAC spoofing — 'Set-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName <VM> -MacAddressSpoofing On' — if the VM uses NIC teaming or a different MAC than the reservation. Also check SR-IOV: Get-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName <VM> | Select IovVirtualFunctionCount
Reset the TCP/IP stack and Winsock: 'netsh int ip reset C:\ip_reset.log && netsh winsock reset' — requires reboot. Modern alternative: Reset-NetIPConfiguration -Verbose

Add Windows Firewall inbound rule if blocking DHCP: 'New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "DHCP Client Allow" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 68 -RemotePort 67 -Action Allow -Profile Any'. Verify existing rules: Get-NetFirewallRule | Where {($_.DisplayName -like '*DHCP*') -or ($_.DisplayName -like '*BOOTP*')}

For post-sleep failures: disable NIC power management — 'Set-NetAdapterPowerManagement -Name "<NIC>" -WakeOnMagicPacket Disabled -D0PacketCoalescing Disabled'. Alternative via Device Manager: devmgmt.msc > Network Adapter > Properties > Power Management > uncheck 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'

For APIPA (169.254.x.x) issues: Check if APIPA is being used correctly or incorrectly. Disable APIPA if not desired via registry: Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters' -Name 'IPAutoconfigurationEnabled' -Value 0 -Type DWord. Reboot required. Note: Microsoft recommends keeping APIPA enabled for fallback

For DHCPv6 issues: Verify IPv6 is enabled on the adapter: Get-NetAdapterBinding -Name '<adapter>' -ComponentID ms_tcpip6. Check if Router Advertisements are suppressing DHCPv6: Get-NetIPConfiguration -Detailed | Select IPv6DefaultGateway,IPv6Address. Disable SLAAC if stateful DHCPv6 required: Set-NetIPv6Protocol -UseTemporaryAddresses Disabled

l1: Run 'ipconfig /all > C:\ipconfig_client.txt' — complete IP configuration including DHCP information. PowerShell alternative: Get-NetIPConfiguration -Detailed | Out-File C:\net_ip_config_detailed.txt

Run 'Get-NetIPConfiguration | Out-File C:\net_ip_config.txt' — PowerShell-based network configuration. For interface-specific: Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias '<adapter>' | Out-File C:\net_ip_config_adapter.txt

Export DHCP Client Operational log: 'wevtutil epl Microsoft-Windows-Dhcp-Client/Operational C:\DHCP_Client_Operational.evtx' — contains DHCP initialization, lease acquisition, renewal, and failure events. Convert to readable format: Get-WinEvent -Path C:\DHCP_Client_Operational.evtx | Select TimeCreated,Id,Message | Export-Csv C:\dhcp_events.csv

Export System event log for network-related events: 'wevtutil epl System C:\System.evtx' — filter for Tcpip, Dhcp, and NDIS events with: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -FilterXPath '*[System[(EventID=4202 or EventID=4206 or EventID=4207)]]' | Out-File C:\system_network_events.txt
l2: Capture DHCP client trace: 'netsh trace start capture=yes tracefile=C:\dhcp_client_full.etl' — reproduce the issue — 'netsh trace stop'. Include provider: 'netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-Dhcp-Client tracefile=C:\dhcp_trace.etl'. Analyze with: tracerpt C:\dhcp_trace.etl -o C:\dhcp_trace.xml
Run 'Get-NetAdapter | Export-Clixml C:\net_adapters.xml' — preserves all adapter properties for later analysis. Include statistics: Get-NetAdapterStatistics | Export-Clixml C:\net_adapter_stats.xml

Run 'Get-NetAdapterBinding | Out-File C:\adapter_bindings.txt' — all protocol bindings. For specific adapter: Get-NetAdapterBinding -Name '<adapter>' | Select DisplayName,ComponentID,Enabled | Out-File C:\adapter_bindings_specific.txt

Run 'Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-Dhcp-Client/Operational | Export-Clixml C:\dhcp_client_events.xml' — event data in XML format. Filter by time range: Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-Dhcp-Client/Operational -MaxEvents 1000 | Where TimeCreated -gt (Get-Date).AddHours(-24) | Export-Clixml C:\dhcp_events_24h.xml

Run 'Get-NetAdapterPowerManagement | Out-File C:\nic_power_management.txt' — power management settings that affect post-sleep DHCP. Include advanced properties: Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty | Out-File C:\nic_advanced_properties.txt
Export TCP/IP configuration: 'netsh interface ip show config > C:\netsh_ip_config.txt' — legacy netsh output for comparison. For IPv6: netsh interface ipv6 show config > C:\netsh_ipv6_config.txt

Collect ARP cache: 'arp -a > C:\arp_cache.txt' — identifies potential IP conflicts. PowerShell: Get-NetNeighbor -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select IPAddress,LinkLayerAddress,State,InterfaceAlias | Export-Csv C:\arp_cache.csv

Export routing table: 'route print > C:\route_print.txt' — shows default gateway and routing. PowerShell: Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select DestinationPrefix,NextHop,RouteMetric,InterfaceAlias | Export-Csv C:\route_table.csv

TSS full data collection: '.\TSS.ps1 -Scenario NET_DHCPcli' — Microsoft Support's TSS (Troubleshooting Script) tool collects comprehensive diagnostics. Download from: https://github.com/microsoft/TSS. Run on the affected client, reproduce the issue, stop when prompted. Output: C:\MSDATA\<timestamp>\

Collect DHCP client registry settings: 'reg export HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters C:\dhcp_registry.reg' — includes APIPA settings, DHCP class ID, and other parameters. Also export adapter-specific: reg export HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces C:\dhcp_interfaces.reg

no_ip_assigned.title: Client not receiving any IP address

steps.action: Get-Service Dhcp | Select Name,Status,StartType,DependentServices
steps.expect: Status: Running, StartType: Automatic. If stopped, run: Start-Service Dhcp; Set-Service Dhcp -StartupType Automatic

steps.action: ipconfig /all
steps.expect: DHCP Enabled: Yes — IP shows 169.254.x.x (APIPA) indicating no DHCP response, or 0.0.0.0 indicating no IP at all. Note the adapter name showing the issue

steps.action: ipconfig /release && ipconfig /renew
steps.expect: Watch for error message — note exact text. Common errors: 'An error occurred while renewing interface', 'The DHCP client has attempted to obtain an address', 'Unable to contact your DHCP server'

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-Dhcp-Client/Operational | Sort TimeCreated -Descending | Select -First 20 | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message
steps.expect: Look for Event ID 1007 (failed to obtain address), 1013 (APIPA assigned), 1006 (lease expired). Events indicate whether DISCOVER was sent and OFFER received

steps.action: arp -a
steps.expect: No duplicate IP-to-MAC mappings — if duplicates exist for the same IP, IP conflict is preventing lease. PowerShell: Get-NetNeighbor | Group-Object IPAddress | Where Count -gt 1

steps.action: Try a different physical switchport or known-good network segment
steps.expect: If IP received on different port/segment, original port has VLAN mismatch, 802.1X authentication issue, or spanning tree blocking

steps.action: Get-NetAdapter | Where Status -eq 'Up' | Select Name,LinkSpeed,MediaType
steps.expect: Link speed should match port capability (e.g., 1Gbps). Check for duplex mismatch causing packet loss

steps.action: Restart-Service Dhcp
steps.expect: DHCP Client service restarts cleanly. Verify with: Get-Service Dhcp | Select Status

steps.action: Restart-NetAdapter -Name '<adapter>' -Confirm:$false
steps.expect: NIC resets — forces fresh DHCP DISCOVER. Identify adapter with: Get-NetAdapter | Where Status -eq 'Up'

steps.action: Disable and re-enable DHCP on adapter: Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias '<adapter>' -Dhcp Disabled; Start-Sleep 2; Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias '<adapter>' -Dhcp Enabled
steps.expect: DHCP reinitialized on the adapter

steps.action: netsh int ip reset C:\ip_reset.log && netsh winsock reset (if above fails)
steps.expect: TCP/IP stack and Winsock catalog reset — requires reboot. Alternative: Reset-NetIPConfiguration -Verbose

steps.action: Update NIC driver from OEM website or Windows Update
steps.expect: Driver updated to latest version. Verify with: Get-NetAdapter | Select Name,DriverVersion,DriverDate

steps.action: ipconfig /all
steps.expect: Valid IP from correct scope, DHCP Server field populated with server IP, Lease Obtained timestamp present (recent), Lease Expires shows future time

steps.action: Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <DHCP_Server_IP> -Port 67
steps.expect: TcpTestSucceeded: True — confirms connectivity to DHCP server

steps.action: ping 8.8.8.8 or known internal server
steps.expect: Successful ping replies — confirms full network connectivity

lease_renewal_failing.title: DHCP lease renewal failing — intermittent APIPA after sleep

steps.action: ipconfig /all before sleep
steps.expect: Document current valid IP, lease obtained time, and lease expires time

steps.action: Put system to sleep (Sleep-Computer), wait 30+ seconds, wake, then run ipconfig /all
steps.expect: IP shows 169.254.x.x (APIPA) or previous lease expired timestamp — confirms renewal failure occurred during sleep

steps.action: Get-NetAdapterPowerManagement -Name '<NIC>' | Select Name,AllowComputerToTurnOffDevice,WakeOnMagicPacket,WakeOnPattern,D0PacketCoalescing
steps.expect: AllowComputerToTurnOffDevice: True means OS is powering off NIC during sleep, which blocks DHCP renewal

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-Dhcp-Client/Operational -MaxEvents 50 | Where TimeCreated -gt (Get-Date).AddMinutes(-30) | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message
steps.expect: Events showing renewal attempt failed (ID 1007) or no response from server after wake. Look for events timestamped after wake time

steps.action: powercfg /energy (run before sleep, capture 60 seconds)
steps.expect: Generates energy-report.html showing NIC power transitions and wake sources. Look for 'USB Selective Suspend' or 'PCI Express' power management affecting NIC

steps.action: Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name '<NIC>' -DisplayName '*Power*' | Select DisplayName,DisplayValue
steps.expect: Check for Energy Efficient Ethernet (EEE) or other power-saving features that may interfere

steps.action: Set-NetAdapterPowerManagement -Name '<NIC>' -AllowComputerToTurnOffDevice Disabled -WakeOnMagicPacket Disabled -D0PacketCoalescing Disabled
steps.expect: NIC power management disabled — NIC stays active through sleep/wake cycles. Verify with: Get-NetAdapterPowerManagement -Name '<NIC>'

steps.action: Alternative via Device Manager: devmgmt.msc > Network Adapters > '<adapter>' > Properties > Power Management > uncheck 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'
steps.expect: GUI method achieves same result as PowerShell. Both methods require elevated permissions

steps.action: Disable Fast Startup if issue persists: powercfg /h off (note: affects hibernation and boot time)
steps.expect: Fast startup can cause NIC to not fully initialize on wake. Test after disabling

steps.action: Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias '<NIC>' -Dhcp Enabled -AutomaticMetric Enabled
steps.expect: Ensure DHCP is re-enabled and automatic metric is set for proper route selection

steps.action: Document current lease info: ipconfig /all | Select-String 'Lease Obtained','Lease Expires'
steps.expect: Note current lease times for comparison

steps.action: Sleep and wake the machine, wait 10 seconds, then run ipconfig /all
steps.expect: Valid IP retained (same as before sleep) or renewed immediately after wake (new Lease Obtained timestamp) — no APIPA (169.254.x.x)

steps.action: Test connectivity: ping <gateway> and ping <external_IP>
steps.expect: Successful pings — confirms network connectivity maintained through sleep/wake

steps.action: Repeat sleep/wake cycle 3 times to verify consistency
steps.expect: IP retained or renewed successfully on all attempts — issue resolved

apipa_persistent.title: Persistent APIPA (169.254.x.x) - client stuck in fallback mode

steps.action: ipconfig /all
steps.expect: IP Address: 169.254.x.x, Subnet Mask: 255.255.0.0, Default Gateway: (blank), DHCP Server: (blank). PrefixOrigin should show 'WellKnown'

steps.action: Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters' -Name 'IPAutoconfigurationEnabled'
steps.expect: Value: 1 (enabled) — allows APIPA. Value: 0 means APIPA disabled, but IP may still be 0.0.0.0 if DHCP fails

steps.action: Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where IPAddress -like '169.254.*' | Select InterfaceAlias,IPAddress,PrefixOrigin
steps.expect: Identifies which adapter has APIPA address. PrefixOrigin: WellKnown confirms APIPA

steps.action: ping <known_DHCP_server_IP>
steps.expect: If ping fails, network connectivity issue exists (VLAN, routing, firewall). If ping succeeds, DHCP service may be down or ports blocked

steps.action: Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <DHCP_server> -Port 67
steps.expect: TcpTestSucceeded: False would indicate UDP 67 blocked by firewall or ACL. Note: Test-NetConnection for UDP may show false negatives

steps.action: Capture network trace: netsh trace start capture=yes tracefile=C:\apipa_trace.etl; ipconfig /renew; netsh trace stop
steps.expect: Analyze trace to see if DHCPDISCOVER is sent and whether DHCPOFFER is received. No OFFER = network/server issue. No DISCOVER = client issue

steps.action: Check switch/router for IP Helper: On Cisco IOS: show ip helper-address | include <VLAN>
steps.expect: Verify IP Helper points to correct DHCP server IP. Missing or incorrect helper = broadcasts not forwarded to DHCP server

steps.action: If IP Helper missing/misconfigured: Configure on router/L3 switch for the client's VLAN. Example Cisco: interface VLAN<X>; ip helper-address <DHCP_server_IP>
steps.expect: DHCP broadcasts now forwarded to DHCP server. Test by renewing lease on client

steps.action: If DHCP server unreachable: Verify server is running: Get-Service DhcpServer on server. Check network path: tracert <DHCP_server>
steps.expect: DHCP server accessible and service running. If server down, start service or restore server

steps.action: If ports blocked: Configure firewall to allow UDP 67/68. Windows Firewall: New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'DHCP Allow' -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 68 -RemotePort 67 -Action Allow
steps.expect: Firewall rules allowing DHCP traffic. Verify with: Get-NetFirewallRule | Where DisplayName -like '*DHCP*'

steps.action: If APIPA should be disabled (e.g., for server or dedicated segment): Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters' -Name 'IPAutoconfigurationEnabled' -Value 0 -Type DWord; Restart-NetAdapter -Name '<adapter>'
steps.expect: APIPA disabled after reboot. Client will show 0.0.0.0 if DHCP fails, making issues more obvious. Note: Microsoft recommends keeping APIPA enabled for most scenarios

steps.action: ipconfig /release && ipconfig /renew
steps.expect: Client receives valid IP from DHCP scope (not 169.254.x.x). Note DHCP Server IP and lease times

steps.action: Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where InterfaceAlias -eq '<adapter>' | Select IPAddress,PrefixOrigin
steps.expect: PrefixOrigin: Dhcp (not WellKnown). IP address matches expected scope

steps.action: ping <gateway> and ping <external_IP>
steps.expect: Successful pings — confirms full network connectivity with DHCP-assigned IP

steps.action: Test after reboot: Restart-Computer; after boot, run ipconfig /all
steps.expect: DHCP IP obtained automatically on boot — no manual intervention required

dhcpv6_issues.title: DHCPv6 addressing problems - stateful vs stateless configuration

steps.action: ipconfig /all
steps.expect: Look for IPv6 Address entries. Note if addresses start with 2001::/16 (global), fd::/8 (ULA), fe80::/10 (link-local), or 2600::/12 (temporary). Check if 'DHCPv6 IAID' and 'DUID' are present

steps.action: Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv6 | Select InterfaceAlias,IPAddress,PrefixOrigin,SuffixOrigin,PreferredLifetime,ValidLifetime
steps.expect: PrefixOrigin: RouterAdvertisement indicates SLAAC. PrefixOrigin: Dhcp indicates DHCPv6-assigned. SuffixOrigin: Random for privacy addresses, Link for EUI-64

steps.action: Get-NetIPConfiguration -Detailed | Select InterfaceAlias,IPv6DefaultGateway,IPv6Address
steps.expect: Shows IPv6 default gateway (link-local of router) and all IPv6 addresses with their origins

steps.action: Capture Router Advertisements: pktmon filter add -p 58; pktmon start --capture; Start-Sleep 60; pktmon stop; pktmon format C:\ra_trace.etl -o C:\ra_trace.txt
steps.expect: Analyze RA packets for M flag (Managed) and O flag (Other). M=1 + O=1 = stateful DHCPv6. M=0 + O=1 = stateless DHCPv6. M=0 + O=0 = SLAAC only

steps.action: Get-NetIPv6Protocol | Select UseTemporaryAddresses,RandomizeIdentifiers,MediaSense
steps.expect: UseTemporaryAddresses: Enabled (privacy addresses). RandomizeIdentifiers: Enabled. These affect which IPv6 addresses are generated

steps.action: Get-NetAdapterBinding -Name '<adapter>' -ComponentID ms_tcpip6 | Select Enabled
steps.expect: Enabled: True — IPv6 protocol must be bound to adapter for DHCPv6 to work. Enable if needed: Enable-NetAdapterBinding -Name '<adapter>' -ComponentID ms_tcpip6

steps.action: On DHCPv6 server: Get-DhcpServerv6Scope -ComputerName <server> | Select ScopeId,Name,State
steps.expect: Verify DHCPv6 scope exists and is Active. Check prefix delegation settings if using IA_PD for subnets

steps.action: If stateful DHCPv6 required but not working: Configure router RA with M=1, O=1. On Windows Server RRAS: netsh interface ipv6 set interface '<interface>' advertise=enabled managed=enabled other=enabled
steps.expect: Router advertisements now signal clients to use stateful DHCPv6. Clients will request IA_NA (address) and IA_PD (prefix)

steps.action: If stateless DHCPv6 desired (SLAAC + DHCP for DNS): Configure router RA with M=0, O=1. netsh interface ipv6 set interface '<interface>' advertise=enabled managed=disabled other=enabled
steps.expect: Clients use SLAAC for IP address and DHCPv6 for DNS server addresses only

steps.action: If SLAAC only desired (no DHCPv6): Configure router RA with M=0, O=0. Disable DHCPv6 scope or set to inactive
steps.expect: Clients self-assign IPv6 addresses via SLAAC only. No DHCPv6 communication

steps.action: Force DHCPv6 renewal on client: ipconfig /release6 && ipconfig /renew6. PowerShell: Remove-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv6 -Confirm:$false; Restart-NetAdapter -Name '<adapter>'
steps.expect: Client sends new DHCPv6 Solicit messages and receives addresses based on current RA flags

steps.action: ipconfig /all
steps.expect: IPv6 addresses present with correct origin. For stateful DHCPv6: addresses from DHCPv6 scope, PrefixOrigin: Dhcp. For SLAAC: addresses based on router prefix, PrefixOrigin: RouterAdvertisement

steps.action: Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv6 | Where PrefixOrigin -eq 'Dhcp' | Select IPAddress,PrefixOrigin
steps.expect: If stateful DHCPv6, one or more addresses with PrefixOrigin: Dhcp. If stateless/SLAAC only, no DHCPv6 addresses

steps.action: Test IPv6 connectivity: Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 2001:4860:4860::8888 (Google DNS IPv6)
steps.expect: TcpTestSucceeded: True — confirms IPv6 Internet connectivity. If fails, check IPv6 routing and firewall

steps.action: nslookup -type=AAAA example.com
steps.expect: Returns IPv6 address (AAAA record) — confirms DNS resolution over IPv6 is working

lease_expiration_conflicts.title: DHCP lease expiration and IP address conflicts

steps.action: ipconfig /all
steps.expect: Note Lease Obtained and Lease Expires timestamps. If Lease Expires is in the past, lease has expired. Check if IP is still usable or if APIPA appeared

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-Dhcp-Client/Operational -MaxEvents 50 | Where Id -in (1006,1007,1010) | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message
steps.expect: Event 1006: lease expired. Event 1007: failed to obtain address. Event 1010: DHCP NACK received (conflict detected)

steps.action: On DHCP server: Get-DhcpServerv4Lease -ScopeId <scope> -ComputerName <server> | Where ClientId -eq '<client_MAC>' | Select ClientId,IPAddress,LeaseExpiryTimes,AddressState
steps.expect: Check if lease exists, its expiry time, and state (Active, Expired, Declined, ActiveOffer)

steps.action: On DHCP server: Get-DhcpServerv4ScopeStatistics -ScopeId <scope> -ComputerName <server> | Select PercentageInUse,Free,InUse
steps.expect: PercentageInUse > 90% indicates scope exhaustion. Need to expand scope or reduce lease duration

steps.action: Check for duplicate IP on network: ping <client_IP>; arp -a | Select-String <client_IP>
steps.expect: If ping succeeds from different MAC, IP conflict exists. Identify conflicting device

steps.action: On DHCP server: Get-DhcpServerv4Scope -ScopeId <scope> -ComputerName <server> | Select Name,LeaseDuration
steps.expect: LeaseDuration determines how long leases are valid. Short leases (e.g., 1 hour) expire quickly if client is offline

steps.action: Check DHCP server conflict detection: Get-DhcpServerv4Setting -ComputerName <server> | Select ConflictDetectionAttempts
steps.expect: Default is 1 (ping once). Higher values increase conflict detection but slow lease assignment

steps.action: If scope exhausted: Expand scope (add more IP addresses) or reduce lease duration: Set-DhcpServerv4Scope -ScopeId <scope> -LeaseDuration <TimeSpan> -ComputerName <server>
steps.expect: More leases available or leases recycle faster. Example: 4 hours instead of 8 days for mobile devices

steps.action: If IP conflict found: Identify conflicting device and remove its static IP or correct reservation. Delete conflicting lease: Remove-DhcpServerv4Lease -ScopeId <scope> -ClientId <conflicting_MAC> -ComputerName <server>
steps.expect: Conflict resolved. Client can now obtain lease without NACK

steps.action: If client lease is stuck in bad state: Delete lease on server and force client renewal: Remove-DhcpServerv4Lease -ScopeId <scope> -ClientId <client_MAC> -ComputerName <server>; On client: ipconfig /release && ipconfig /renew
steps.expect: Fresh lease obtained. Client should get same or different IP depending on availability

steps.action: Create DHCP reservation for critical clients: Add-DhcpServerv4Reservation -ScopeId <scope> -IPAddress <IP> -ClientId <MAC> -Name '<description>' -ComputerName <server>
steps.expect: Client always receives same IP, prevents conflicts and lease expiration issues for static devices

steps.action: ipconfig /all
steps.expect: Valid IP assigned, Lease Obtained is recent, Lease Expires is in future (typically 50% of lease duration later)

steps.action: On DHCP server: Get-DhcpServerv4Lease -ScopeId <scope> -ClientId <client_MAC> -ComputerName <server> | Select AddressState,LeaseExpiryTimes
steps.expect: AddressState: Active, LeaseExpiryTimes shows future expiry time

steps.action: Test connectivity: ping <gateway>; ping <external_IP>
steps.expect: Successful pings — confirms IP is unique and routing is working

steps.action: Monitor for renewal: Wait until T1 (50% of lease), check event log for Event ID 1003 (lease renewed)
steps.expect: Lease renewed automatically without user intervention. Confirms healthy DHCP operation
